 1          Plaintiffs CITIBANK, N.A. (“Citibank”) and CITIGROUP GLOBAL MARKETS INC.

 2   (“CGMI”) (collectively, “Citi” or “Plaintiffs”) file this Complaint against defendants JOHN A.

 3   MITCHELL (“Mitchell”) and BENJAMIN C. CARR (“Carr”) (collectively, “Defendants”), and

 4   allege as follows:

 5                                        Preliminary Statement

 6          1.      This action is for a temporary restraining order and a preliminary injunction to

 7   maintain the status quo pending resolution of an arbitration proceeding between Citi and

 8   Defendants before FINRA Dispute Resolution.1

 9          2.      On July 19, 2024, Defendants gave notice of their resignation of employment

10   from Citi. Defendants resigned in concert with fifteen other former Citi employees. Due to

11   contractual obligations, Mitchell was required to give 75-days advance written notice of his

12   intention to resign from Citi – during which he would continue to be employed by Citi. Thus,

13   Mitchell’s resignation became effective and his employment with Citi terminated on October 2,

14   2024, after which he immediately became affiliated with BMO Wealth Management, which, on

15   information and belief, is a division of BMO Capital Markets Corp. (“BMO”) (along with the

16   other fifteen former Citi employees).      Carr provided two weeks’ written notice, and his

17   resignation became effective August 2, 2024. On information and belief, Carr also joined BMO

18   after October 2, 2024. At the time of their resignations, Mitchell was a Private Banker and

19   Banker Team Lead in the Law Firm Group of Citi Global Wealth at Work, and Carr was a

20   Private Banker under Mitchell who worked in the Law Firm Group of Citi Global Wealth at

21   Work. Both Mitchell and Carr worked at Citi offices in San Francisco, California.

22
     1
       The Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (“FINRA”) was created in July 2007 through the
23
     consolidation of the National Association of Securities Dealers, Inc. and the member regulation,
24   enforcement and arbitration functions of the New York Stock Exchange. Citi has the express right
     to seek temporary injunctive relief before a court of competent jurisdiction pending the outcome of
25   arbitration before a full panel of duly-appointed arbitrators pursuant to Rule 13804 of the FINRA
     Code of Arbitration Procedure for Industry Disputes. A true and correct copy of Rule 13804 is
26   attached to this Complaint as Exhibit B. On October 28, 2024, Plaintiffs commenced an
27   arbitration against Mitchell (and others) before FINRA Dispute Resolution as a result of Mitchell’s
     improper conduct in soliciting Citi employees during his Citi employment to leave Citi and join
28   BMO. Citi is in the process of amending such arbitration claim to add Carr as a respondent.

 1           3.      Defendants entered into agreements with Citi and have obligations to Citi

 2   requiring them to maintain the confidentiality of Citi’s confidential and proprietary business and

 3   client information after their employment with Citi ends. This agreement is required of most all

 4   Citi employees in the United States.

 5           4.      Since Defendants’ employment with Citi terminated and they joined BMO, Citi

 6   has learned that Defendants likely took or retained confidential and proprietary information

 7   relating to Citi and its clients and are using it at BMO.

 8           5.      Specifically, on information and belief, Defendants took or retained, among other

 9   information, confidential and proprietary information relating to the cash positions and products

10   held by Citi clients they formerly serviced, including information relating to the maturity dates of

11   Certificates of Deposits held by Citi clients.

12           6.      On November 4, 2024, Mitchell sent an email, as a BMO employee, to a Citi

13   client he formerly serviced comparing the current interest rates for a Certificate of Deposit

14   (“CD”) being offered by BMO and Citi, stating that the deposit rates he can offer at BMO “are

15   better than Citi.”    Most alarmingly, Mitchell sent this email to the Citi client specifically

16   referencing the client’s “high cash position” and on the exact day – November 4, 2024 – that the

17   client’s multi-million dollar CD at Citi matured. That is, the very day the client had to decide

18   whether to “roll-over” her CD at Citi, Mitchell “appeared” to offer the client a purportedly more

19   attractive offer with BMO.

20           7.      The client forwarded to Citi a copy of Mitchell’s November 4, 2024 email, a copy

21   of which is attached to this Complaint as Exhibit A (with the client’s name, email address and

22   employer information, as well as the CD rates offered, redacted). The email Mitchell sent to the

23   client states as follows:

24                   I hope this finds you and the family doing well. I’m now at BMO
                     Private Bank and was hoping to connect to discuss our strong Private
25                   Bank platform and relationship with [CLIENT EMPLOYER
                     REDACTED]. Are you amendable to a call this week or next?
26

27                   I also wanted to share the deposit rates I can offer are better than
                     Citi. I thought this was especially relevant given your high cash
28

 1                  position. See below and let me know if you have any questions.
                    (Exhibit A, emphasis added.)

             8.     Citi is greatly concerned that Defendants have sent – or will send – similar emails
 3
     to other Citi clients on or about the maturity dates of their Citi CDs offering to help them with
 4
     purportedly better CD rates at BMO, using information they improperly took or retained from
 5
     Citi.
 6
             9.     On information and belief, there is no way that Defendants could be aware of the
 7
     client’s cash balances and the maturity dates of the CD without taking or retaining such
 8
     confidential and proprietary information from Citi upon their departure. It strains credulity to
 9
     believe that it is simply a coincidence that Mitchell sent the Citi client this email comparing
10
     BMO CD rates to Citi CD rates on the exact date that the client’s CD matured and was set to
11
     renew without the use of Citi confidential and proprietary information, which he is not permitted
12
     to use or retain after his employment ended.
13
             10.    On July 17, 2024 – less than 48 hours before Defendants gave notice of their
14
     resignations, Carr engaged in highly unusual activity on Citi’s internal computer system by
15
     running three different types of searches – one search was done three times, for a total of five
16
     searches – on Salesforce (Citi’s customer relationship management platform), including a search
17
     for “my clients.” The information accessed by Carr on July 17, 2024 is highly confidential,
18
     including Citi client lists and identifying Citi clients who had large cash balances. The
19
     information obtained by such search would have indicated the names of Citi clients and at a
20
     minimum, their cash balances. On information and belief, the client to whom Mitchell sent the
21
     email attached hereto as Exhibit A – who was assigned to Carr and also known to Mitchell – was
22
     one of the clients contained in at least two of the reports accessed by Carr (including the “my
23
     clients” search).
24
             11.    Prior to accessing this detailed client information just two days before giving
25
     notice of his resignation, Carr had not accessed any of these files on Salesforce at any point from
26
     June 24 through July 16, 2024 (June 24 was the farthest back that Citi was able to search). Thus,
27
     it is apparent that Carr’s search two days before he resigned was not done in the ordinary course
28

 1   of business while working on behalf of Citi. There was no legitimate reason for Carr to access

 2   this information at that time.

 3          12.     On information and belief, Carr took such client information with him from Citi to

 4   his new firm (by some means of capture or duplication, whether by taking photos of the computer

 5   screens with his cell phone, copying, or via some other means), and Mitchell used such information

 6   at BMO to try to convince a Citi client to move their CD to BMO.

 7          13.     At the time of his resignation, Mitchell was responsible for overseeing

 8   approximately 450 law firms and their partners/associates at Citi, with a total of approximately

 9   $497 million in assets. All of these relationships formerly serviced by Mitchell were assigned by

10   Citi’s Law Firm Group to Mitchell to service.

11          14.     At the time of his resignation, Carr serviced approximately 570 law firms and

12   their partners/associates at Citi, with a total of approximately $152 million in assets. All of these

13   relationships formerly serviced by Carr were assigned by Citi’s Law Firm Group to him to

14   service.

15          15.     Defendants’ conduct constitutes a breach of their agreements with Citi, which

16   contain confidentiality provisions, and a violation of their common-law obligations to Citi.

17          16.     To prevent continued irreparable harm arising from Defendants’ course of

18   misconduct, Citi seeks immediate injunctive relief (in the form of a temporary restraining order

19   and a preliminary injunction) barring Defendants from further using and compelling the return of

20   Citi’s confidential and proprietary business and client information, pending resolution of Citi’s

21   claims in a related arbitration that Citi has commenced.

22                                        Jurisdiction and Venue

23          17.     The Court has jurisdiction in this action pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1332(a) in that, as

24   alleged below, Plaintiffs, on the one hand, and Defendants, on the other hand, are citizens of

25   different states, and the matter in controversy exceeds the sum or value of $75,000, exclusive of

26   interest and costs.

27          18.     Venue is proper in this judicial district pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1391(a), in that a

28   substantial part of the events giving rise to the claims occurred in San Francisco, California.

27   for Citi that provides a suite of wealth management services – from investments to lending,

28   banking and family wealth planning – to professionals (i.e., lawyers, accountants, tech

 5          25.     A typical Law Firm Group client will be assigned a Banker, such as Carr (to take

 6   care of their banking and lending needs), an Investment Counselor (to provide investment

 7   advice), a Financial Planner (to develop a long-term investment strategy) and a Wealth Planner

 8   (to address trust and estate needs).

 9          26.     Citi typically assigns a Banker (who is generally the point person on the team),

10   such as Carr, to several law firms in a geographical area. Citi’s relationship with every law firm

11   is different. For many law firms, Citi has a business relationship with the firm itself, as well as

12   with individual partners/associates.       For many law firms, Citi may be the “preferred”

13   banking/investment firm for individual partners/associates; for others, Citi may be on a short list

14   of banks/investment firms that are recommended to individual partners and attorneys by the firm.

15          27.     Citi’s Law Firm Group serves more than 900 law firms across the country,

16   including almost all of the law firms within the top 200 (as ranked by The American Lawyer).

17   Citi has had a longstanding business relationship with a significant percentage of these law firms

18   for many years, and in many cases, the relationship has existed for decades.

19          28.     Thus, Citi Bankers in the Law Firm Group – which includes some of the other

20   individuals who left with Defendants and who are being targeted by BMO – are not tasked with

21   seeking out and securing new law firms as clients; indeed, they are prohibited from doing so.

22   Rather, Law Firm Group Bankers are tasked solely with servicing Citi’s pre-existing law firm

23   clients. As indicated above, Citi has a strong banking/investment relationship with many of these

24   law firms, as well as being a preferred or recommended bank/investment firm to their

25   partners/associates.

26          29.     As part of their official duties at Citi, Defendants had access to extensive

27   confidential financial records and information about Citi’s clients, including information about

28   each client’s investment needs. As explained in further detail below, such information – which is

                    will have a continuing obligation not to use, publish or otherwise
20                  disclose such information either during or after your employment
                    with the Company. (Exhibit C at 1.)

     not to use, disclose, or retain any Citi confidential information after his employment with Citi

     ends:

                    You must never use (except when necessary in your employment

                    confidential or unpublished information you obtain as a result of your

                    employment with us. This applies both while you are employed with

 1                                   Citi’s Confidential Information

 2          42.     During the course of their employment with Citi, Defendants had access to Citi’s

 3   highly confidential customer files and other information that is confidential and proprietary.

 4          43.     Citi’s customer records contain confidential financial information regarding each

 5   client, including client names, addresses, telephone numbers, email addresses, transactional

 6   history, tax information, personal financial data, banking information and investment objectives,

 7   among other data. On information and belief, Defendants had no interaction with the vast

 8   majority of the clients they serviced at Citi (and no knowledge of their confidential information)

 9   until they started working at Citi. This information has been collected at great expense to the

10   firm, is not easily duplicated, and would be extremely valuable to Defendants to use at a

11   competitor firm such as BMO.

12          44.     Citi’s records concerning its customers are not publicly available or available

13   from other sources and have been created and updated for a period of many years based on Citi’s

14   relationship with its clients. Citi has invested substantial corporate resources to develop and

15   maintain its customer and employee information.

16          45.     Citi has invested substantial time and money, totaling millions of dollars, to

17   acquire, develop and maintain its customers over many years. It is with great difficulty, and only

18   after a great expenditure of time, money and effort, that Citi was able to acquire its existing

19   clients. Citi spends substantial resources in gaining knowledge about its clients and protecting

20   the privacy of such information. It typically takes many years of dealing with clients for Citi to

21   become their primary bank or investing firm. Citi clients typically remain with and continue to

22   be serviced by the firm, regardless of whether team members resign or leave Citi. But for

23   Defendants’ employment with Citi, they would not have had any contact with the vast majority

24   of the clients they serviced at Citi. Defendants had no prior brokerage or financial services

25   industry experience prior to joining Citi and spent their entire careers with Citi until their

26   resignations. Thus, on information and belief, Defendants brought no clients with them to Citi

27   from a prior employer.

28          46.     The confidential, proprietary, and trade secret information that, on information

10   to its customers’ information to only those employees working directly with such clients or and

11   certain management supervising those employees, in addition to only a limited number of other

12   employees who need access to such information.

13          48.     Citi’s customers are the lifeblood of its business. The expenditures incurred by

14   Citi in obtaining its clients include the many thousands of dollars spent by Citi every year on

15   national and local advertising, the millions of dollars it costs to train the Citi sales force, the

16   millions of dollars a year Citi spends for sales support staff, clearing services, operations

17   personnel, systems and support, management and compliance supervision, salaries, annual

18   registration fees, computer services and equipment, phone, mail, research, literature, seminars,

19   trade and other professional news publications, promotional events, the retention of experts, and

20   the many other expenditures Citi incurs in maintaining its goodwill in the financial industry. Citi

21   has borne the entire expense of these services and activities as well, with no financial

22   contribution from Defendants.

23          49.     Employees such as Defendants must maintain such customer information as

24   strictly confidential. These instructions are confirmed in the various agreements and provisions

25   referenced above.
